 How Investors May Respond To Grab Holdings (GRAB) AI Infrastructure Deal
 MI Mitch Lawler November 12, 2026, 07:38 UTC Share Grab Holdings announced that it has joined SoftBank Group and Petroleum Sarawak Berhad in joint development agreements to build AI infrastructure in Malaysia, backed by US$1.85b in proposed initial seed capital across Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.
 The structure gives Grab a leading role in the Peninsular Malaysia AI project with US$650m of proposed seed funding. This positions its core platform closer to high-demand compute capacity that could influence future operating costs and service capabilities.
 We will look at how Grab Holdings' AI infrastructure push with SoftBank may reshape the earlier investment narrative around cash generation.
 Scan beyond Grab Holdings' AI push and spot other potential beneficiaries of rising compute demand with our hand picked list of 53 AI infrastructure stocks .
 Advertisement Grab Holdings Investment Narrative Recap
 For shareholders, the basic belief is that Grab Holdings can keep turning a large user base into steadily better unit economics in deliveries, mobility and financial services while managing capital intensity. According to John_Eric, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the key near term catalyst is cleaner, stronger free cash flow. The AI infrastructure push adds another cash hungry project, so the main question is whether these commitments slow that cash reacceleration.
 The biggest risk John_Eric flags is already high non cash earnings, which can make headline profit less useful as a guide. Multi year AI build outs funded with US$750m of Grab capital raise execution and funding questions, although staged deployment and project level financing should help. In the short term, investors will likely still focus on whether core operations and Financial Services move closer to consistent cash generation.
 The recent third quarter 2026 report is the most helpful anchor for thinking about this AI move. Grab posted group sales of US$1,112m for the quarter and US$27m of net income, with basic EPS at US$0.01. Over the first nine months of 2026, revenue reached US$3,064m and net income US$415m, which supports the idea in John_Eric’s piece that there is a healthier business under the earlier accounting noise.
 Set against that backdrop, committing US$750m of seed capital to Malaysian AI infrastructure looks like a swing that leans on that improving earnings base. The raised 2026 revenue guidance to a range of US$4.15b to US$4.20b suggests management sees operating traction, but the execution test now widens. Investors tracking catalysts may focus on whether future quarters show AI spending being matched by project milestones and customer contracts, without stalling progress on free cash flow and Financial Services breakeven.
 On John_Eric’s numbers, that US$5.90 fair value reflects a story in which Grab Holdings grows revenue about 22.0% a year and eventually settles at a future profit margin near 16.0%. Together, these assumptions support his view that today’s operations can justify a higher long run earnings power.

 NasdaqGS:GRAB 1-Year Stock Price Chart Exploring Other Perspectives
 Some analysts saw the big risk for Grab Holdings very differently. You might focus on cash generation, while the most cautious forecasts before this AI deal assumed revenue of about US$6.5b and earnings near US$771.4m by 2029, with margins tightening. Those estimates already looked wary. This AI infrastructure push could change that story again, in either direction, so it is worth comparing several viewpoints side by side.
